column1: # .github/failopen-allow.tsv — every site the fail-open rules fire on that is
# An allowance is NOT a lowered severity. Every rule in api/cmd/failopenlint
# is an error and stays one; a row here records a verdict and the reasoning
# behind it, exactly as .github/sast-register.tsv does for gosec.
#   deliberate      the pattern is real and intended, with a stated tradeoff.
#   blocked         real, and the fix waits on the issue cited. These are what
#                   get revisited when the fix becomes available, which is the
#   false-positive  the rule fired and the code is correct. The reasoning must
#                   say WHY, specifically enough that the next reader need not
# A row is keyed on rule + path + symbol, never on a line number. For FO04 and
# FO07 the symbol carries the variable name too, so an allowance covers one
# setting rather than everything the function happens to read.
# The gate FAILS on an allowance that matches nothing any more: a row that
# outlives its site is a permission nobody granted.

column6: reasoning

The named exception: this is the TOFU capture that reads a BMC's certificate so the operator can confirm its digest before it is stored as a pin. There is nothing to verify against yet, which is the whole purpose of the call.
A stored BMC selection can still opt out of verification. Retired with the rest of the insecure selections when the BMC moves onto the one pinned-TLS helper.
Same selection, applied at construction. Retired by the same change.
The backend honours the insecure selection and the pin-only mode through the same field. Retired by the same change.

This IS the pinned-TLS helper the rule names. Verification is not skipped, it is moved: VerifyConnection compares the peer's SPKI against the pin and fails the handshake on any mismatch, which is stricter than chain verification. The file carries a trip-wire comment saying the same thing at the line.
The discarded error can only leave healthy false, which is the closed outcome: the sink refuses the write, records the result and returns an error to its caller. Nothing is lost to the operator.
Same shape and same direction: a readiness probe that errors reports the stack as not ready, which is what the snapshot already shows while the stack is starting.
Nothing to delete, for the same reason. The early return is not a skipped authorization check: no caller reaches it with an authenticated session.

An empty token means the request carried no session cookie. Returning no session is the closed outcome — the caller treats a nil session as unauthenticated — and looking up the hash of an empty string would match nothing anyway.
Nothing to touch. The statement updates rows matching the token's hash or the token, and an empty token matches no row; the early return only avoids the query.
The write-only slot's contract: an empty value means 'keep the stored one', because a form that did not re-type the password is not asking to clear it. Clearing is a separate act, not an empty write.
